correctness.rationale: The spectral theorem reduces the self-adjoint matrix norm to top-k absolute eigenvalue sums. The dual vector ball is the intersection of a coordinate cube and an l1-ball of integral radius k; its vertices are exactly k-coordinate sign supports. On each such vertex, F=I-11^T/n has dual norm max of its largest absolute coordinate and its l1 norm divided by k. Writing the sign sum d reveals a discrete concave quadratic; its maximum is attained either at d=k (value 2-2k/n) or at the single-opposite-sign bound (value 1+(k-2)/n). Diagonal explicit primal witnesses attain both branches in their regimes. Averaging any real-linear projection over unitary/orthogonal conjugation gives the unique equivariant projection C, establishing global minimality. Boundaries n=2, k=1 and k=n are included. Exact rational enumeration through n=10 corroborates the universal proof.

value.rationale: A motivated sharpness gap follows explicitly from an already published, rank-independent Ky Fan estimate for a canonical spectral projection. The new exact expression is uniform over all matrix dimensions and Ky Fan ranks, gives a natural two-mechanism phase boundary, explicit equality inputs, complete norm-one exceptions, and an optimal-rank limiting value of 4/3. This is a complete natural invariant classification, not an arbitrary numerical table or a routine change of notation.
